claims.text: Four customers have events at times 2 and 4, and censoring at 3 and 5. What is Kaplan–Meier survival just after time 4? Options: 0; 0.375; 0.5. Toy model: compare two controlled cases.

claims.text: Three at risk; one event, then one censor, then an event. Final KM survival? After the censor, the last event removes the sole remaining at-risk person.

claims.text: Keeping the at-risk sets gives survival 0.375 after time 4. Dropping censored customers before calculation gives 0 instead.

claims.text: The first event removes 1 of 4 at risk. Censoring at 3 removes someone from later risk sets; the event at 4 removes 1 of the remaining 2. Kaplan–Meier multiplies 3/4 by 1/2. Its usual interpretation requires appropriate non-informative censoring.
